I think I understand better, now. It's a logic issue. The prompts inherently guide discourse toward their topics.

There are other concerns as well. In a standard thread, thoughts are filtered quickly, dissenters fall to the bottom, popular answers rise, and the thread is eventually bumped after a day or so havong exhausted all interest. Later, the question can be asked again. In these stickied posts, the same answer filtering happens, but due to the increased exposure, the thread becomes more polarized and stale. No new discussion takes place because the signal to noise ratio grows too high. A simpler alternative might judt be to allow quicker reposting of questions(this is, admittedly, more of a community issue, however.).

The polarization is still inherent when you have a voting system. A mass of voters in will tend to vote for similar opinions. A better way to prevent polarization would be to change the voting system itself. Reposting the question is a terrible answer as certain opinions would always get voted up.

As it is, stickied content is a wrong direction. If the community were interested in the questions they would naturally rise to the top. Prioritizing content is generally not a good idea.

Forget about the polarization for a moment and consider what the primary principles of /v/askgoat were at its creation in response to mod meddling and the shaping of content at /v/AskVoat. There are two rules here: don't break site rules, and ask a question (sort of). I know stickied questions seem benign(and your question really is currently) but it does more than simply provide an open platform for discussion, and if nothing else, it violates the principles of the subverse. The sub's mods shouldn't be here to tell us what to discuss(no matter how innocuous), they should be here to clean up the trash.

Edit: I should mention that I absolutely encourage mods to continue making regular posts, after all, tons of really interesting questions are posted by the mod team every week. They really keep things moving and contribute quite a bit to the community as users.
